 Coram: Honourable Justice Smt. Anjana Prakash
 Oral Order
2/ 27-02-2013
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

The Petitioner seeks bail in a case instituted for the offence under Section(s) 414/34 Indian Penal Code, Sections 26(i)
(iv), 31, 42, 48, 50 of Food Safety and Standard Act and Section 2, 3, 4 of Exchange Act.

Considering that the Petitioner is in custody since 24.12.2012 and there is no other case pending against him, let the Petitioner, above named, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.5,000/-(Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each or any other surety to be fixed by the Court below to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Saran at Chapra, in connection with Awtarnagar P.S. Case No.128 of 2012, subject to the conditions (i) That one of the bailors will be a close relative of the petitioner, who will give an affidavit giving genealogy as to how he is related with the petitioner and another bailor shall be Shashi Bhushan Kumar, son of the Petitioner.

The bailors will undertake to furnish information to the court about any change in the address of the petitioner, (ii) That the affidavit shall clearly state that the petitioner is not an accused in any other case and, if he is, he shall not be released on bail, (iii) That the bailors shall also state on affidavit that they will inform the court concerned if the petitioner is implicated in any other case of similar nature after his release in the present case and thereafter the court below will be at liberty to initiate the proceeding for cancellation of bail on the ground of misuse, (iv) That the petitioner will give an undertaking that he will receive the police papers on the given date and be present on date fixed for charge and if he fails to do so on two given dates and delays the trial in any Baiju Prasad Chaurasiya vs The State Of Bihar on 27 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152884291/
1 manner, his bail will be liable to be cancelled for reasons of misuse, and (v) That the petitioner will be well represented on each date and if he fails to do so on two consecutive dates, his bail will be liable to be cancelled.
 JA/- (Anjana Prakash, J)
Baiju Prasad Chaurasiya vs The State Of Bihar on 27 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152884291/
